idiom_name: Vapor Middleware + Authenticatable with req.auth.require / guardMiddleware
implementation_notes: Vapor's Middleware protocol is the enforcement point: an authenticator middleware logs the verified principal into req.auth, and a guard - User.guardMiddleware() or a custom middleware that inspects req.auth - rejects the request before the route handler runs, while handlers call req.auth.require(User.self) and fail loudly when the identity is missing. Authorization beyond identity (roles, ownership) belongs in one middleware or policy type consulted by a route group applied with app.grouped(...), so every route under it inherits the check; Vapor deliberately keeps authentication and authorization separate, which makes that layer the place to decide. Composed groups mirror the enforcer chain: authenticator, then guard, then the decision.
pitfalls: Authenticator middleware alone does not reject: without guardMiddleware (or an explicit throw) the route runs unauthenticated, which Vapor documents as intentional composability.
Middleware added after routes were declared does not protect them; build the guarded group first and register routes on it.
Storing the principal on mutable shared state instead of req.auth leaks identity across the concurrent requests an event loop serves.
